title: His Own Instagram Helped the FBI Identify Hushpuppi
central_question: How did an influencer's own Instagram help the FBI identify him?
content_notes: Closed federal case: Abbas pleaded guilty (April 2021) to one count of conspiracy to engage in money laundering and was sentenced in November 2022 to 135 months; he is serving the sentence. Narration states only what he pleaded to. The victims (companies and individuals) are never shown or named; no co-conspirator, police officer or other person is named. Separate allegations (e.g. claims involving a Nigerian police officer) are omitted. Abbas appears only as an anonymous rim-lit silhouette or from behind (not a likeness, never one of his own photos or his booking photo). The phone feed, jet, cars, apartment and offices are generic drawings: no Instagram/Snapchat logo or interface, no car badges, no airline or police insignia, no real usernames, email addresses or phone numbers (masked). Every card is our own typed graphic. No dialogue is invented. Legal status verified 2026-10-12.

lines.text: He posed with jets and luxury cars on Instagram.
His own account helped the FBI identify him.
Ramon Abbas, Hushpuppi, had over two million followers.
He later admitted conspiring to launder money from online scams.
Agents got his Instagram records: an email and a phone number.
They matched a Snapchat contact an accomplice had saved as Hush.
And his posts matched his passport photos.
In June 2020, Dubai Police raided his apartment and handed him to the FBI.
He pleaded guilty to a money laundering conspiracy,
and got more than eleven years in prison.

claims.text: Ramon Abbas ('Hushpuppi') posted his lavish lifestyle on Instagram: court papers describe posts of him in designer clothes and expensive watches, posing in or with luxury cars and charter jets; CNN cites Rolls-Royces.
Ramon Abbas is known on social media as Hushpuppi (also 'Ray Hushpuppi').
His Instagram account had more than two million followers (BBC: 2.5 million; CNN: more than two million).

Per the FBI affidavit (as reported), agents obtained Instagram's records for his verified account, which listed an email address and a verified phone number; the account helped investigators identify him. (Email and number are never shown.)

Per the affidavit, the same email was on the Snapchat account 'hushpuppi5', which was linked to a number an accomplice had saved in a phone as 'Hush'; his Instagram also mentioned that Snapchat name. (No co-conspirator is named.)
Per the affidavit, agents matched photos posted on his accounts to photos from his passports and other identification documents.
Dubai Police arrested Abbas in June 2020 after raids including his Dubai apartment; police said they seized cash and 13 luxury cars (amounts reported differently, so not narrated).
FUN FACT (card only): Dubai Police called the operation 'Fox Hunt 2'.
Dubai Police handed him to the FBI, and FBI agents brought him to the United States in early July 2020 (DOJ: expelled, not extradited); he first appeared in court in Chicago on 3 July 2020.
In April 2021 he pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to engage in money laundering, laundering money from business email compromise and other online fraud schemes.
In November 2022 U.S. District Judge Otis D. Wright II sentenced him to 135 months (over 11 years) in federal prison and ordered $1,732,841 in restitution.
Status (12 Oct 2026, research only): the Ninth Circuit dismissed his petition for review in January 2024; fact-checks in February 2026 found no release, with a projected release in 2029.
